packets.lens: Would a model actually route to this agent, and would a human understand what came back?
packets.instructions: Execute the prompt once per subject below. Return a JSON object mapping each subject's `slug` to that subject's answer object, exactly in the shape the prompt specifies. Add nothing else. Then hand the file to `sentinel.py absorb`.
packets.prompt: You are reviewing one entry in the AIBAST Agents Library — either a single-file agent (Python) or an aggregated skill (Markdown). Read what it says it does, how it is invoked, and what it hands back. Answer only these questions. (1) If twenty entries were loaded at once, would a model pick this one for the task it claims? Say what it would be confused with. (2) Is what it returns something a human can act on, or does it need interpretation the entry should have done itself? (3) Name the single edit that would most improve routing accuracy. Be concrete and quote the text you are judging. Do not praise. Return JSON: {routing_risk: low|medium|high, confusable_with: string, return_value_verdict: string, single_best_edit: string, teachable: string}.

packets.lens: Does the agent do what it says, or does it describe doing it?
packets.instructions: Execute the prompt once per subject below. Return a JSON object mapping each subject's `slug` to that subject's answer object, exactly in the shape the prompt specifies. Add nothing else. Then hand the file to `sentinel.py absorb`.
packets.prompt: You are reviewing one entry in the AIBAST Agents Library — a single-file agent (Python) or an aggregated skill (Markdown). Determine whether its behavior matches its claims. A demo that returns a scripted response, or a skill that describes an outcome it never produces, is legitimate ONLY if it says so plainly and says it first. A description implying live data while the implementation returns a fixed string is misrepresentation — that is the defect you are looking for. Return JSON: {claims_live_data: boolean, returns_fixed_response: boolean, misrepresents: boolean, evidence: string, teachable: string}. Set misrepresents=true only when you can quote both the claim and the contradicting implementation.

packets.lens: What is the worst thing that happens to someone who installs this?
packets.instructions: Execute the prompt once per subject below. Return a JSON object mapping each subject's `slug` to that subject's answer object, exactly in the shape the prompt specifies. Add nothing else. Then hand the file to `sentinel.py absorb`.
packets.prompt: You are reviewing one entry in the AIBAST Agents Library for installation risk — a single-file agent (Python) or an aggregated skill (Markdown) that a model will execute. Assume the operator is a non-expert running it against their own tenant. Enumerate what it writes, deletes, sends, or spends — not what it reads. For each, state whether it confirms before acting and whether the action is reversible. Ignore stylistic issues entirely. Return JSON: {writes: [string], irreversible_actions: [string], spends_money: boolean, confirms_first: boolean, worst_case: string, teachable: string}.

packets.lens: Can someone learn the pattern from reading this?
packets.instructions: Execute the prompt once per subject below. Return a JSON object mapping each subject's `slug` to that subject's answer object, exactly in the shape the prompt specifies. Add nothing else. Then hand the file to `sentinel.py absorb`.
packets.prompt: You are reviewing one entry in the AIBAST Agents Library as TEACHING material — the library is how people learn to build on the Microsoft AI stack, so a published entry is read far more often than it is run. Identify the one pattern it demonstrates best and the one thing in it a newcomer would wrongly copy. Return JSON: {pattern_demonstrated: string, worst_thing_to_copy: string, suitable_as_example: boolean, teachable: string}.
